description.narrative:
- Cooperation and coordination between involved partners Oxfam serves as Lead Applicant and Secretariat of the consortium, ensuringeffective coordination, quality assurance, and compliance with donor requirements. Oxfam consolidates annual work plans and budgets, manages donor liaison, leads policy influence at the national level, and oversees external evaluations and audits. In addition, Oxfam facilitated capacity building among consortium partners on donor compliance, safeguarding, financial and grant management, knowledge sharing, and communities of practice, ensuring that all partners operate according to common standards and strategic objectives. The consortium partners—including API, SILAKA, DPA, NGOF, YRDP, and CamboJA—work collaboratively across different components of the project. Each partner contributes complementary expertise in areas such as civic engagement, social accountability, digital governance, youth mobilisation, public financial management, media engagement, and GRB. Theconsortium will meet quarterly to coordinate implementation, review progress against the work plan and results framework, identify risks and adaptations, and validate joint policypositions and advocacy messages. These meetings also serve as a platformto consolidate learning and ensure alignment between local implementation activities and national-level policy dialogue. Oxfam ensure the coordination of the following interventions:
- The intervention approach/methodology/instruments The design ofthe CLIPS intervention is intended to complement the EU-SCOPE PFM. There are some similar or the same activities, but the target locations are different. This is to ensure the efficient use of available resources to achieve greater impact. CLIPS: The detailed activities are attached in the Annex: logframe and activities matrix. Outcome 1: Capacity and Participation Outcome statement: Strengthen the capacity of citizens and sub-national administrations to access, understand, and use budget informationand digital participatory tools for effective engagement in local fiscal decision-making. Strategic Intervention: The project will build the capacity of citizens and responsive local authorities by combining structured capacity building, institutionalstrengthening, and digital engagement. This integrated approach simultaneously increases citizen capability, institutional readiness, and access to information.  Establish a standardized and scalable capacity-building system by working with SNAs andNCDDS to develop harmonised training manuals, facilitation tools, and a coordinated project kick-off process. This ensures consistency, quality, and alignment with national governance frameworks, creating a strong foundation for civic engagement.  Create adecentralised “community of trainers” model by pooling expertise from implementing partners and specialised organisations. This approach maximises reach without overstretching resources and ensures that different target groups (youth, women, PwD,journalists) receive tailored, high-quality training.  Strengthen citizen capacity for informed participation through targeted training for community groups and CBOs on fiscal management, participatory budgeting, monitoring, and advocacy. This enables citizens to meaningfully influence commune and district investment planning processes.  Enhance institutional capacity of sub-national authorities (SNAs) through training on participatory public financial management, inclusive planning, and accountability.This ensures that authorities can effectively facilitate citizen engagement and integrate community priorities into decisionmaking.  Promote evidence-based budget advocacy and responsiveness by supporting SNAs to use budget analysis and structureddialogue to advocate for increased and more inclusive resource allocation.  Scale the use of digital participation tools through awareness campaigns on existing public financial management applications (e.g., Citizens Budget, ISAF App) Outcome 2:Accountability and Oversight Outcome statement: Strengthen citizen-led monitoring and accountability mechanisms to track public expenditure, promote transparency, and improve government responsiveness. Strategic Intervention: The project will operationalise accountability by shifting trained citizens from passive participants to active leaders of oversight and advocacy processes through citizen initiatives and activities that generate evidence and engage directly with government platforms.  Enablecitizen-led accountability through community-driven initiatives by supporting trained groups, youth networks, and CBOs to design and implement their own civic actions on budgeting, service delivery, and governance. These initiatives include participation in budget planning processes, monitoring procurement, conducting budget analysis, and producing publicaccountability content.  Institutionalize participatory monitoring practices by embedding community engagement in formal planning and decision-making spaces such as Commune Investment Plans (CIP), District Development Plans (DDP), and council meetings.  Generate and use evidence for advocacy and accountability through action research and monitoring reports produced by citizens and shared with sub-national authorities, strengthening data-driven dialogue and responsiveness.  Embed civic engagement culture among youth andcommunities by integrating civic engagement into school curricula and community work plans. This includes training teachers and students, supporting school-led debates, and fostering youth-led initiatives on fiscal governance. Outcome 3: Institutionalisation and Sustainability Outcome statement: Institutionalise inclusive, transparent, and responsive mechanisms within sub-national administrations for sustained citizen participation. Strategic Intervention: The project will transition from project-driven engagement to system-level institutionalisation of participatory governance. These interventions ensure that participation-related policies and practices are revised, tested, and implemented to promote effective civic participation in local budget/fiscal management.  Strengthen policy frameworks for civic engagement in PFM by reviewing and updating existing civic guidelines to integrate digital participatory approaches into local fiscal management systems.  Support implementation of revised policies and guidelines by SNAs, ensuring that participatory practices are embedded in routine governance processes rather than remaining ad hoc.  Facilitate structured and recurring council–citizen dialogue mechanisms through joint learning forums where fiscal data is analysed collaboratively, and actionable budget adjustments are identified.  Promote peer learning andreplication across communes and districts through exchange visits, documentation, and dissemination of good practices, enabling scaling and long-term sustainability.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
